data.body:
CLOSING — not building this now (decision, 2026-07-24).

No MCP client has asked for a caller-facing `sign` opt-out. Today the only thing that
suppresses MCP signing is the server's own read-only mode, and that path works. Adding the
parameter plus a machine-readable unsigned reason is a real public-API change (tool schema +
generated reference) with no current consumer, so it is not worth carrying as open work.

Recorded for whoever revives it: the design fork is WHERE the unsigned reason lives — a new
field on the shared review result (more useful, but a shape change every consumer sees) versus
MCP-local (safer, less useful). The shared-result option is probably right, because the same
"signed=false with no stated reason" ambiguity exists on the CLI and library routes too.

Closed WITHOUT completion verification (force-close): nothing was implemented, so there is no
work to verify. The closed-without-signature state is the accurate signal here.
